system.name: PVM
system.one_liner: a high-performance guest hypervisor for KVM that hosts secure containers without requiring hardware nested-virtualization support

components.name: L2 (non-root mode ring0)
components.role: L2 guest kernel, handles page faults via its PF Handler and owns GPT2

components.name: GPT2
components.role: L2's guest page table, made read-only to L2 so updates trap for shadow-table synchronization

components.name: L1 (non-root mode ring0)
components.role: L1 guest hypervisor kernel, maintains the shadow page table for L2

components.name: KVM PF Handler
components.role: L1's handler that injects faults into L2 and builds shadow mappings

components.name: SPT12
components.role: shadow page table mapping L2 guest virtual addresses directly to L1 physical addresses

components.name: VMCS12
components.role: VM control structure for the L1-L2 transition

components.name: L0 (root mode ring0)
components.role: host hypervisor dispatching between VMCS01 and VMCS02 and maintaining EPT/CR3

components.name: VMCS01
components.role: VM control structure L0 uses to run L1

components.name: VMCS02
components.role: VM control structure L0 uses to run L2

components.name: CR3
components.role: page-table base register switched on world switches

components.name: EPT
components.role: extended page table mapping guest physical to host physical addresses

components.name: EPT_violation Handler
components.role: L1's handler for EPT violations in the EPT-on-EPT approach

components.name: EPT12
components.role: L1-maintained EPT-format table mapping L2's guest-physical addresses to L1 physical addresses, read-only

flows.what: trap back to L0 to resume L2

content.key_idea: Panel (a) SPT-on-EPT has L1 maintain a software shadow page table synchronized with L2's page table via trapped page faults; panel (b) EPT-on-EPT instead lets L1 maintain its own EPT-format table so hardware two-dimensional paging can be nested; both require multiple trap-and-resume steps across L0/L1/L2.
content.reading_order: Left panel (a) SPT-on-EPT first, top-down through L2, L1, L0 following circled steps 1-9; then the same privilege-level structure in the right panel (b) EPT-on-EPT.

encoding.emphasis: identical L2/L1/L0 scaffolding in both panels lets the circled step sequences visually demonstrate that EPT-on-EPT and SPT-on-EPT both require long chains of trap-and-resume steps across privilege levels

As illustrated in Figure 3 (b), L2 has its own GPT2, which maps GVAL2 to GPAL2

summary: This two-panel figure compares SPT-on-EPT (a) and EPT-on-EPT (b), the two existing approaches to 2-level nested memory virtualization. Both panels share the same L2/L1/L0 privilege-level scaffold. In (a), L2's guest page table GPT2 is made read-only so its updates trap; L1's KVM PF Handler combines GPT1 and GPT2 into a shadow page table SPT12, and a page fault is traced through nine circled steps as it bounces between L2, L0 (via VMCS01/VMCS02), and L1 (via VMCS12) before GPT2 is finally updated and control returns to the L2 user. In (b), L1 instead maintains its own EPT-format table (EPT12, read-only) and handles EPT violations directly, letting L0 use hardware two-dimensional paging. Both panels are dense, gray flat-filled box diagrams with circled step numbers (32 in total) tracing the expensive world-switch chains that motivate PVM's alternative design.
summary_zh: 该图并排比较两种两级嵌套内存虚拟化方案：(a) SPT-on-EPT 中 L1 通过陷入合并影子页表；(b) EPT-on-EPT 中 L1 维护只读 EPT 供硬件两维分页使用，两者均需在 L2/L1/L0 间经历多步跳转。
notes: Context text for panel (b) EPT-on-EPT is truncated right after it begins, so panel (b)'s components and flows are inferred mostly from labels visible in the compact preview image rather than from prose, unlike panel (a) which the text walks through step by step.
